reverseBrief.humanQuestion: What do the different AI labels mean, and what do I need to understand so I can use AI deliberately and understand what is happening behind an app or claim?
reverseBrief.promisedPayoff: A types-first, connected plain-English map from AI labels through physical systems and model training, with direct concept lookup.
reverseBrief.centralMentalModel: AI labels classify different properties; an AI system then connects product, information, model, optional tools, physical infrastructure and people, while training shapes the model and inference uses it.
reverseBrief.dailyLifeConnection: Meeting notes, expense claims, party planning, voice notes and a leave-policy question show the same mechanisms in recognisable life and work.
reverseBrief.surfaceJob: The opening of a durable nine-chapter LIBRAiRY explanation plus a compact Concept Index, not a glossary or class transcript.
reverseBrief.desiredReaderFeeling: Oh, I get it now—and I can use this map somewhere else.

explainBack.observation: A simulated cold-reader probe can recover type axes, generative/agentic, system/model/product and training/inference distinctions from the draft.

artifactEvidence.locator: Chapter 1 — Generative and agentic describe different things

simulatedReaderProbe.prompt: Without using the book's wording, distinguish generative AI, agentic AI and AGI; then explain the difference among an AI product, model and system and training versus inference.
simulatedReaderProbe.probeResponse: Generative AI produces content; agentic AI continues through steps and may use tools; AGI is a disputed proposed threshold for broad transferable capability, not another word for an agent. A product is the interface and surrounding software, a model is a learned component, and the system includes both plus information, infrastructure, controls and people. Training adjusts the model; inference uses it.
simulatedReaderProbe.expectedEvidence: Separates the three labels, names the three system levels and separates parameter change from model use.

unseenTransfer.observation: A simulated transfer probe can classify a new product across non-exclusive axes and locate its system parts.

artifactEvidence.excerpt: No single label describes the whole product.
artifactEvidence.locator: Chapter 1 — Put one product on the map

simulatedReaderProbe.prompt: A tool listens to a sales call, drafts a summary, updates the customer record and schedules a follow-up. Classify it by job, modality, method, breadth and operating pattern without calling it AGI.
simulatedReaderProbe.probeResponse: It transcribes, classifies and generates; moves from audio to text; likely uses machine learning and deep learning; may use a general-purpose model inside a specialised sales product; and is agentic if it continues through permitted updates and scheduling steps. None of that establishes AGI.
simulatedReaderProbe.expectedEvidence: Uses several non-exclusive axes, separates generative from agentic and does not infer AGI from multi-step action.
